# What Builder sends, and what it does not

Builder reads the logs your AI coding tools already write to your own disk. Almost all of
that never moves. This page is generated directly from the file that defines the network
payload, so it cannot drift from the code: if a field is not in this table, the app has no
way to represent it on the wire.

## Never leaves your machine

Your prompts. The model's replies. Its thinking. Anything you or the model typed into a
file. Diffs and patches. File contents. **File paths, and file names.** Directory names.
Commit messages. Commit SHAs. Branch names. Your working directory. Your git remote URL.
The names of repositories you have not marked public. MCP server names. Terminal commands
and their output. Environment variables. URLs fetched. Your hostname. Your IP.

Not redacted versions of these. Not excerpts. There is no code path that sends them.

## What does leave, if you sign in

Every field, in full. `1` is the contract version.

| Field | Type | Sent for | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_session_id` | sha256hex | public + anonymous | stable opaque session id; also the Idempotency-Key |
| `machine_id` | sha256hex | public + anonymous | sha256 of this Mac's platform UUID |
| `content_hash` | sha256hex | public + anonymous | hash of this payload; lets sync skip unchanged sessions |
| `client_version` | string | public + anonymous | agent version |
| `sessionizer_version` | int | public + anonymous | so a retuned boundary is a recompute, not a migration |
| `active_calc_version` | int | public + anonymous | so a retuned active-time formula is a recompute |
| `harness` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `agent_observed_at` | datetime | public + anonymous | when the agent finalized this session |
| `client_clock_offset_ms` | int | public + anonymous | measured against the server Date header |
| `started_at` | datetime | public + anonymous |  |
| `ended_at` | datetime | public + anonymous |  |
| `active_seconds` | int | public + anonymous | union of turn spans and capped gaps; the honest headline |
| `idle_seconds` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `tz_offset_minutes` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `time_quality` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `state` | enum | public + anonymous | only final sessions are ever uploaded |
| `visible` | bool | public + anonymous | counts toward hours, graph, streaks |
| `notable` | bool | public + anonymous | eligible for a card or a record |
| `strip_columns` | base64 | public + anonymous | 1024 bytes: 2-bit class, 2-bit density. No text, no paths, by construction |
| `strip_marks` | marks | public + anonymous | [{ms, k}] where k is prompt|commit|compact |
| `timeline_fidelity` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `human_prompt_count` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `prompt_count_basis` | enum | public + anonymous | so Cursor's looser rule never sums with Claude Code's |
| `tool_calls` | toolmap | public + anonymous | allowlisted tool names only; unknown and MCP names bucket to mcp_other / other |
| `files_touched` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `files_created` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `lines_added_agent` | int | public + anonymous | live-path only; rewound edits never landed |
| `lines_removed_agent` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `commit_count` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `commit_insertions` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `commit_deletions` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `human_edit_events` | int | public + anonymous | count of edited_text_file / humanChanges signals. Existence only — these carry no line counts |
| `agent_line_bucket` | enum | public + anonymous | a 5-way LOWER BOUND, never a percentage |
| `attrib_confidence` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `tokens_reported` | bool | public + anonymous | false for EVERY Cursor session, forever — Cursor never writes token counts locally |
| `tokens` | tokens | public + anonymous | five separate buckets. Null, never zero, when unreported |
| `abandoned_branch_tokens` | int | public + anonymous | tokens spent on rewound DAG branches. You paid for them |
| `token_dedupe` | enum | public + anonymous | server rejects none + tokens_reported: that is the 1.88x arriving unlabeled |
| `token_scope` | enum | public + anonymous | 'flat' is NOT a legal value — it would let the ~3x subagent glob overcount in wearing a legitimate label |
| `token_coverage` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `models` | models | public + anonymous | [{model_id, output_token_share}] — labels only. The [1m] suffix is preserved verbatim |
| `model_state` | enum | public + anonymous | Cursor is ~84% unknown: modelName is 'default' on 115 of 137 composers |
| `repo_hash` | sha256hex | public + anonymous | HMAC of the normalized origin URL. Full 64 hex, never truncated |
| `repo_pepper_version` | int | public + anonymous |  |
| `repo_id_basis` | enum | public + anonymous |  |
| `repo_name` | string | **public repos only** | PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. Absent from the anonymous key set entirely |
| `title` | string | **public repos only** | PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. The title the HARNESS already wrote to your disk. Never model-generated by us |
| `title_source` | enum | **public repos only** |  |
| `card_png_url` | url | public + anonymous | populated ONLY when you tap Share. The image you chose to publish; contains no field not listed above |

## Per-repository control

Every repository is **anonymous** by default: its sessions sync as a shape and a set of
counts, with no name attached. You can set a repository to **public** — which adds only
`repo_name`, `title` and `title_source` — or to **excluded**, which sends nothing at all.
If a single session touched an excluded repository, the whole session is dropped rather
than partially uploaded.

Titles come from the title your coding tool **already wrote to your disk**. Builder does
not send your prompts to a model to generate one. There is no such endpoint.

## Check it yourself

Do not take the above on faith. The agent is open source and these commands run locally.

```bash
# 1. Print every byte the agent would send. Sends nothing.
builder sync --dry-run --print-payload | jq

# 2. Diff its actual keys against this page, in both directions.
#    `leaf_paths` expands the four structured fields (tokens, models, strip_marks,
#    tool_calls) so a scalar-path walk lines up exactly. tool_calls keys are tool
#    names, so they are normalised to the wildcard the contract publishes.
builder sync --dry-run --print-payload \
  | jq -r '[paths(scalars)] | .[] | join(".")' \
  | sed 's/^sessions\.[0-9]*\.//' \
  | sed 's/\.[0-9][0-9]*\./\./g' \
  | sed 's/^tool_calls\..*/tool_calls.<allowlisted tool name>/' \
  | sort -u > /tmp/actual
curl -s "$BUILDER_BASE_URL/upload-fields.json" | jq -r '.leaf_paths[]' | sort -u > /tmp/declared

# Anything on the left that is not on the right is a field we send and did not declare.
comm -23 /tmp/actual /tmp/declared

# 3. Pick a phrase you typed to your agent today. Go looking for it.
builder sync --dry-run --print-payload | grep -i "that phrase"   # no output, exit 1

# 4. Trust none of the above. Builder does not certificate-pin, on purpose.
mitmproxy -p 8080 &
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8080 builder sync
```

## Repository hashing: the honest limit

Repositories are identified by an HMAC of the normalized git origin URL. The key is a
**global constant, identical for every user** — matching the same repository across two
machines requires both to derive the same hash. It ships inside an open-source binary and
is **not secret**.

The hash defeats casual exposure and makes a database dump unreadable. It does **not**
survive a dictionary attack against public repository names. If you need real secrecy, set
the repository to `excluded`: it is never hashed, never uploaded, and never parsed again.
Private set intersection is the correct fix and is not built.

## Permissions

Builder does not require Full Disk Access, Screen Recording, or Accessibility, and does not
ask for them. It reads `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor` and Cursor's application support
directory, none of which are protected by those permissions today. If a future macOS release
restricts one of them, Builder will tell you which one and why, and will keep working on the
others.
